families.label: Make & tinker
families.blurb: Small parts, hands-on projects, and the satisfaction of making something work.

families.label: Nature & outdoors
families.blurb: From a windowsill to a mountain path, notice more of the world around you.

families.label: Stories & imagination
families.blurb: Read, watch, collect, and bring fictional worlds into your own.

families.label: Play & collect
families.blurb: Games to share, systems to understand, and old favourites worth keeping.

families.label: Food & everyday rituals
families.blurb: Make a meal, refine a recipe, or turn your morning cup into an experiment.

families.label: Sound, images & signals
families.blurb: Make music, tell a story on screen, or discover what travels through the air.

examples.label: Coffee
examples.title: From espresso to lightsabers.
examples.blurb: An espresso-machine project opens into electronics and custom lightsabers. Follow the shared craft, or take a side path into sound.
notes: Espresso connects to the hobby of modifying the machine that brews it.
Custom pixel sabers draw on the same electronics craft.

branch.note: Electronics also opens into modular synthesizers.

examples.label: Miniatures
examples.title: Build a world. Then let it grow.
examples.blurb: The eye for a miniature landscape carries into terrariums, houseplants and propagation. Another branch takes the scenery underwater.
notes: Dioramas and terrariums both compose a landscape at a small scale.
Terrariums connect to the wider world of keeping houseplants.
Growing houseplants can lead into propagating and sharing them.

branch.note: Terrariums connect to aquascaping: landscapes under water.

examples.label: Birdwatching
examples.title: From garden birds to distant galaxies.
examples.blurb: An interest in birds can lead through photography to the night sky. The same camera craft can turn toward something as close as dinner.
notes: Birdwatching connects to the craft of photographing what you observe.

branch.note: Food photography draws on the same camera craft.

starters.core.photography: Photograph one everyday object from five angles using a phone and window light. Choose the frame that tells the clearest story.
starters.core.writing: Describe a familiar place in 150 words without naming it. Ask a friend what they pictured, then revise one detail.
starters.core.painting: Mix three shades of one colour and paint them on scrap card. Notice how the same colour changes beside a lighter or darker patch.
starters.core.programming: Make a tiny script that picks a random item from a list of your interests. Change the list and explain each line in your own words.
starters.music.guitar: Choose two chords you already know or want to learn. Change between them slowly for five minutes, listening for each string to ring clearly.
starters.coffee.espresso: Keep the beans and dose fixed for a few cups. Record the output weight and how each tastes before changing just one variable.
starters.coffee.pourover: Use a brewer you already have. Weigh the coffee and water for one cup and write down what you would change next time.
starters.garden.houseplants: Observe one plant for a week. Note where the light falls and how the potting mix changes between waterings before adjusting its care.
starters.garden.bonsai: Sketch the trunk and main branches of a tree you can see. Look for its strongest line before thinking about how you might shape a bonsai.
starters.garden.herbs: Pick a herb you already use in cooking and learn its light and watering needs. Start with one pot and a place you will see every day.
starters.maker.arduino: Open the built-in Blink example on a board you already have or in a simulator. Change the timing, then explain what each delay does.
starters.maker.cad: Model a simple box with dimensions taken from an object on your desk. Change one measurement and see which parts of the design follow it.
starters.model.gunpla: Choose one small section of a kit, such as an arm. Read the whole section first, build it unpainted, and notice how the pieces locate each other.
starters.figure.mini-painting: Try a three-colour scheme on one spare figure or a sketch of it. Keep the shapes readable before adding tiny details.
starters.rail.layout: Draw a small layout on paper and trace the movement of one train. Check that each track has a purpose before adding another.
starters.brick.moc: Build something recognisable from just 20 pieces you already own. The limit is a useful way to notice new uses for familiar parts.
starters.cosplay.armour: Sketch one small costume piece and make a paper mock-up. Check how it moves with you before choosing a final material.
starters.tabletop.boardgames: Play a familiar game and name the one decision that makes it interesting. Teach that decision first the next time you explain the rules.
starters.tabletop.ttrpg: Invent a place, someone who wants something there, and a problem in their way. That is enough material for a short scene with a friend.
starters.book.fiction: Read the opening pages of a book you already own. Note the moment you first wanted to know what happens next, and what caused it.
starters.film.horror: Revisit a scene from a film you know. List what the sound tells you before anything frightening appears in the frame.
starters.anime.mecha: Compare two robot designs from a series you enjoy. Sketch the silhouettes and ask how each design suggests a different role.
starters.outdoor.hiking: Choose a familiar short walk and look at its route on a map first. Afterwards, compare the map with the landmarks you noticed.
starters.outdoor.birdwatching: Watch one bird from a respectful distance for five minutes. Record its shape, movement, sound, and surroundings before trying to name it.
starters.kitchen.baking: Repeat a recipe you already know, weighing the ingredients this time. Write down one observation about the dough or batter before it goes into the oven.
starters.kitchen.cooking: Cook a familiar dish and write down the order of its steps. Next time, prepare the ingredients in that order and notice what becomes easier.
starters.video.editing: Cut five short clips into a 30-second sequence with a beginning and an ending. Watch it without sound to check whether the order still makes sense.
starters.astro.visual: From a familiar observing spot, sketch the positions of three bright stars. Return another evening and compare where they appear.
starters.game.gamedev: Sketch a game with one action and one goal. Build a paper version of its rules before deciding what needs to be on a screen.
starters.retro.consoles: Pick a game you remember and document its controls, sound, and one detail you had forgotten. Start a small record of why it is worth preserving.
